To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. Word embedding models maximize a mutual information lower bound 2. The lower bound is a function of the word embedding objective function 3. We provide an analysis of the word embedding model objective function that shows it is a function of a mutual information lower-bound.

1) the mutual information between two parts of a word sentence is a lower bound for the objective function of all state of the art language representation learning methods, 2) this perspective unifies classical word embeddings and contextual word embeddings, 3) our derivation leads to the development of a novel self supervised objective that can be used for representation learning and 4) our framework offers a holistic view for representation learning methods across different domains.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a novel theoretical understanding of language representation learning methods and propose a novel self supervised learning objective.

we are able to show that the objective function used by the state of the art language representation learning methods is a lower bound for the mutual information between two different parts of the word sequence, and we can derive a principled framework to construct new self-supervised objectives by drawing inspiration from other domains.
we provide a new perspective on the existing word embedding methods by showing that they are all maximizing a lower bound on mutual information between different components of a word sequence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the objective of learning representations from unlabeled data is to maximize the mutual information between the learned representations and the data.
representation learning methods are all about maximizing mutual information between different representations of the same data.
mutual information maximization can be used to design new self supervised tasks that are complementary to the existing ones.
